display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Git is required, and bundled as MinGit, so nothing is installed
Parallel work, checkpoints, undo, export as branches and
crash recovery are Git features. Plain copies, Jujutsu and
per-file editor snapshots do not replace them in v1
Mercurial or Perforce: not supported. Offer Work on a copy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer picks a folder. The checkout is their desk
The harness never edits, stashes, resets or commits there
without an explicit click

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What is in the folder?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Silent git init, branch main
The Phase 0 commit is scanned before it is made

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Set up Git, or work on a copy?
There is no continue-without-Git

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before any baseline or snapshot: scan .env files, private keys,
high-entropy tokens, files over 50 MB, node_modules, build
output and OS junk. Show the .gitignore proposal and the
secrets that will not be committed. Accept, edit or cancel

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Copy into a new folder and set up Git there

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Record HEAD and the branch as the project base

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: You have uncommitted files

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Warn that landing may later need those files committed

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Wait, then recheck

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No commits yet. The baseline is shown before it is made

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Merge, rebase, cherry-pick or conflicts: block.
Open in my editor. Never finish or abort it
Detached HEAD: pick a branch, or create harness-base and the date
OneDrive, Dropbox or a network folder: warn, continue or move
No user.name or email: one prompt, globals prefilled
Git missing from PATH: the bundled Git is used

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What is being recorded?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Show what the baseline commit includes, then make it

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Dirty work is snapshotted, never moved. Stash is not used
Temporary index: GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree HEAD, add -A,
write-tree, commit-tree with parent HEAD,
store refs/harness/snapshots, then drop the temp index
Working tree, real index and branch stay untouched
The scan runs on the snapshot diff first. That commit is the workers' base
A later identical developer commit merges cleanly

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer's branch: landing target, only by a visible landing
harness/integration: accepted, tested work
harness/f/feature: private while its tasks land
harness/t/task/attempt: one leased attempt
refs/harness/checkpoints: WIP, kept for resume and export
Author is the role and agent id. Committer is the developer
Trailers: Harness-Task, Harness-Attempt
A human fix keeps the human as author

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Worktree outside the project, under LOCALAPPDATA
git worktree add --detach, then the attempt branch
core.longpaths. Registered on the attempt lease
Ignored files are absent, so the environment manifest supplies them
Secrets: env from the vault, never files
Local config: an allowlist copy. Dependencies: the lockfile,
with a shared package cache. Submodules init. LFS only for
the task's paths. Sparse checkout when the brief declares it
After retention: remove the worktree and prune
Checkpoint refs survive until the feature lands or the user deletes them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Windows: short worktree root. Optional Defender exclusion
Keep .gitattributes, or the developer's autocrlf
Workers never rewrite line endings
Flag two paths that differ only by case
Stop the attempt's Job Object before deleting a locked tree
Predict a landing with git merge-tree --write-tree, before touching anything

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Existing repo, or a new one?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Folder is ready. Discovery uses the opening prompts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Opening card from a local scan. Zero tokens spent
What would you like to change?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Read cheaply, ask the model last
L0, free: tree, languages, manifests, scripts, tests, CI,
docs, schema, migrations, .env.example names, Git churn
L1, free and local: tree-sitter symbols, reference graph,
entry points from routes, main and bin
L2, bounded and cached by blob hash: one module card
per area this request touches. Show the estimate first
L3, per task: exact files or spans at the pinned commit
The message chooses the L2 modules. The rest stay at L0 or L1
L0 and L1 never leave the machine. Mask secrets before L2
A local-only project uses a local model, or skips L2

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Five change prompts, prefilled from the scan and the message
What changes. Which part, and who uses it. One done example
What must not change. How you check it today
A mixed message splits. Separate readiness, shared project facts
Slow is not testable. Ask the page, today's number, and the target
Recommended default: p95 under 300 ms on a realistic dataset
Trace the route to the query. Seeded data or a sanitized dump
Record EXPLAIN ANALYZE or a timing harness
Acceptance: a Tier 3 benchmark, plus that page's existing tests

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Confirmation card, not a lecture. Source and confidence on each claim
Tick, correct or ignore. Confirmed claims become observed facts
A correction overrides the observation and links to it
Unreviewed claims stay observed, unconfirmed
High-confidence ones may be used. A medium one used by a task
is listed in that task's assumptions
Stale docs: code wins for today. Never rewrite the README
unless a task includes it. Conventions node is quoted into briefs
Canvas: Today in grey, Change in color, edges show what is touched

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Run install, build and tests
in an isolated copy?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Baseline receipt

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Not measured. Every later acceptance still runs
a pre-change baseline for the checks it touches

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Targeted checks pass, and no new failures anywhere

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Known failing, by name. No new failures
Optional task to fix those. Workers are not blamed for them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Unstable. Out of pass or fail until the owner stabilizes them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Safety net first. A test runner only with approval
Characterization tests for the touched modules,
passing before and after

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Stop. Offer Make the build pass. Feature work waits

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deleted worktree: fence it, recreate from the last checkpoint
gc or prune: refs survive, missing worktrees are recreated
Repo moved: relocate, then git worktree repair
Huge repo: measure, then lower parallelism or use sparse checkout
Shallow clone: worktrees work. Skip blame hotspots
Monorepo: ask which packages, and scan those deeply
Generated or vendored: out of maps and write scopes
Unsupported language: L0 stays, L1 is text search,
L2 uses the files the request names
A request that contradicts the schema is a planned change
New commits during discovery: pin the start commit,
refresh changed cards before planning
